prompt:
Check one candidate model relation against sentences of a long engineering document. Unit ids show the order of the sentences in the document; the sentences come from different places.

Candidate: primary workspace provides "Common Situation Display" to Regional Flow Manager (an information or material flow).

Evidence sentences used to propose the candidate:
S116: The Airport Duty Manager may request a manual capacity review when local observations differ materially from the automated weather interpretation.
S117: The Regional Flow Manager uses the Common Situation Display to compare forecast demand, assessed capacity, and any active Ground Delay Program effects in one operational view.
S152: Access to the Airport CDM Portal is controlled by the Identity Access Service so that each user sees only the workspaces, aircraft, stands, and decision records appropriate to the assigned role.
S153: The primary workspace presents the Common Situation Display with synchronized clocks, active operating state, airport demand, runway configuration, stand occupancy, and milestone status for each managed movement.
S337: The Airport CDM Portal displays the active restriction status, expected operational effect, and any related coordination notes on the Common Situation Display.
S338: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the shared display to identify flights that may need rerouting, delayed pushback planning, or revised operator intent.
S870: The Slot Coordinator shall receive training on the Slot Allocation Engine, Airport CDM Portal, and applicable Business Rules Registry entries so that slot actions are applied consistently and transparently.
S871: The Network Operations Liaison and Airspace Sector Planner shall be trained to coordinate regional constraints, sector load conditions, and network measures using the Sector Load Monitor and Common Situation Display.

Other sentences of the same document that mention this item, a similarly named item, or another element that produces or sends such an item:
S020: The Common Situation Display is expected to give authorized users a shared view of demand, capacity, constraints, and active traffic management measures.
S046: The shared operational picture includes Flight Intent Message status, Airport Capacity Plan assumptions, Target Off Block Time values, Calculated Takeoff Time values, Airport Acceptance Rate constraints, Common Situation Display content, Tactical Regulation Proposal status, Collaborative Decision Log entries, and Post Operations Report outputs.

S088: The Airport Duty Manager is the primary airport escalation contact and confirms that airport-side constraints are reflected consistently across the Airport CDM Portal and the Common Situation Display.
S095: The Departure Metering Service and Arrival Regulation Console are used only under the authority of the accountable flow roles, and their outputs must remain visible on the Common Situation Display.
S130: Accepted intents are reflected on the Common Situation Display as proposed airline actions until the Regional Flow Platform reconciles them with airport and airspace constraints.
S144: The Airport Duty Manager monitors the Common Situation Display to ensure airline recovery decisions remain consistent with terminal capacity and passenger processing conditions.
S165: The Common Situation Display distinguishes values supplied by connected services, values confirmed by users, and values that have exceeded the configured freshness threshold.
S265: The Common Situation Display shows the current agreed target set so that operational participants can see whether a flight is proposed, under negotiation, frozen, or exempted from compliance monitoring.
S366: When a predicted queue exceeds the warning threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub highlights the affected runway queue on the Common Situation Display.
S391: The Common Situation Display highlights expired treatments, pad closures, fluid shortages, and ramp blockages so that participants can resolve conflicts without separate status calls.
S400: The Capacity Assessment Module calculates candidate Airport Acceptance Rate values for each runway configuration and exposes the operational basis for each value on the Common Situation Display.
S421: The Common Situation Display provides the base map, timeline, flight list, and measure status panels used at the position.
S422: The Regional Flow Platform synchronizes the tactical display with the Time Synchronization Service so that all timestamps, countdowns, and validity intervals use the same operational clock.
S425: The Tower Supervisor uses the display to see runway assignment pressure, airborne sequence spacing, and expected crossing points at the North Runway Meter and the South Runway Meter.
S440: A Tactical Regulation Proposal can be drafted directly from the display, checked against current capacity assumptions, and routed through the Alert Distribution Hub for stakeholder acknowledgement.
S462: The Common Situation Display highlights active surface advisories with the affected stands, taxi segments, runway meters, and flight identifiers visible to authorized users.
S527: The Airport CDM Portal keeps detailed handler notes available to authorized users while the Common Situation Display shows only the flight impact, severity, and expected recovery window.
S560: The Common Situation Display presents remote stand status in time order so that airline, ramp, tower, and airport roles share the same expectation for aircraft readiness.
S613: All converted measures are displayed on Common Situation Display with the source constraint, effective interval, affected runway or fix, and expected delay impact.
S627: Common Situation Display shows crew legality impacts as coded operational states, such as feasible, time critical, infeasible, or operator review required.
S685: The Common Situation Display presents the updated Calculated Takeoff Time and Target Off Block Time so that operational users share the same view of the accepted change.
S704: The Common Situation Display shows the affected resource, start time, review time, and current decision status using language that can be understood by operational staff.
S729: The Arrival Regulation Console may continue to display arrival demand, but the Regional Flow Manager approves any arrival regulation changes through direct coordination.
S758: The Common Situation Display presents passenger disruption cues with clear labeling so that participants understand they are decision-support indicators, not commands.
S822: Freshness indicators shall be displayed on the Common Situation Display wherever stale data could affect sequencing, metering, regulation, or resource allocation decisions.
S885: Workstation layouts shall support rapid comparison between the Common Situation Display, Airport CDM Portal, Tower Sequence Manager, Ramp Movement Board, and relevant advisory messages without forcing users to copy critical values manually.
S952: These options should be generated by the Contingency Operations Console and reviewed through the Common Situation Display before any operational decision is applied.

Answer "supported" only if the document states that primary workspace produces or sends this item AND that Regional Flow Manager receives or uses the same item (it may be named more briefly in one sentence), and no other sentence shows that the item Regional Flow Manager uses comes from a different producer or is a different item with a similar name. Answer "unsupported" if the sentences describe different items, the wrong elements, the opposite direction, or if another producer of the item the consumer uses is stated. Answer "uncertain" if the text is not clear enough. Return JSON {"verdict": ..., "reason": "one sentence"}.
response: {"verdict":"supported","reason":"S153 says the primary workspace presents the Common Situation Display, and S117 says the Regional Flow Manager uses that display; no other sentence names a different producer or a different item with a similar name."}
